explain.say: Imagine sitting in a quiet room when suddenly your tummy goes grrrumble! Everyone hears it. What's going on in there? Look at the body on the board. Your stomach and intestines are tubes with muscle walls that squeeze to move food along.

explain.say: See the air bubbles? Along with food and drink, there's gas and air you swallowed. When the muscles squeeze, the gas is pushed through the tubes and gurgles, like water glugging down a drain. Can you make a gurgling sound?

explain.say: Look at the small intestine. When your tummy is empty, a cleaning wave of squeezes sweeps through about every hour and a half to two hours, clearing out leftovers. With no food to muffle it, the gas echoes loudly. That's why hungry tummies are the noisiest!

faq.q: Why does my tummy rumble when I'm hungry?
faq.a: When your stomach is empty, waves of muscle squeezes sweep through to clear it out. Gas and liquid get pushed along, and with no food to muffle them, they gurgle loudly.

faq.q: How does my body know I'm hungry?
faq.a: When your stomach has been empty for a while, it releases a hormone called ghrelin. Ghrelin travels in your blood and tells your brain you need food.

faq.q: Does my tummy only rumble when I'm hungry?
faq.a: No. It rumbles while digesting too, but food in the gut muffles the noise, so you notice it more when you're empty.
asks: Why does my tummy gurgle after eating?

faq.q: What is the scientific name for tummy rumbles?
faq.a: Borborygmi. One single rumble is a borborygmus.

faq.q: Where does the gas in my tummy come from?
faq.a: Some is air you swallow when you eat, drink or talk, and some is made by helpful bacteria breaking down food in your gut.
asks: Why is there air in my stomach?

facts: Tummy rumbling sounds are called borborygmi.
Ghrelin, a hormone made mainly by the stomach, signals hunger to the brain.
